research_question: Can training QFourier models with a fixed differentiable surrogate fitted to the Q.ANT periodic response reduce reference-to-Q.ANT prediction disagreement and improve Q.ANT accuracy compared with exact-cosine training?
observations: Exp012 output-noise training did not reduce disagreement.
Exp013 found structured mismatch that increased with Fourier frequency.
Exp014 showed that bfloat16 explains only part of the mismatch and that a structured Q.ANT residual remains, especially at higher frequency and nonzero phase.
hypothesis: A fixed differentiable periodic surrogate fitted to Q.ANT calc_kan_layer_fprop will reduce prediction disagreement versus exact-cosine training on locked QFourier architectures, with the largest benefit expected for g8.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is not supported if surrogate-aligned training fails to reduce mean prediction disagreement for both g4 and g8, or if any disagreement reduction is accompanied by a material decrease in mean Q.ANT accuracy.

proposed_method.surrogate: fixed periodic lookup/interpolation response fitted before model training from Q.ANT CPU-backend scalar samples; differentiable linear interpolation during training; no trainable surrogate parameters

limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
The surrogate is fitted to numerical CPU-backend behavior and should not be interpreted as a physical optical model.
The experiment tests whether response alignment improves deployment agreement, not whether the surrogate is the unique or optimal approximation.
